title: Novakai Messaging — public contract source (Step 2)
authority: Messaging-Ratification.md §9/§10; Messaging-Store-Seam.md §6 (and its §11 errata). This file is the SINGLE source of truth for every contract shape (law #3). Docs, validators, and the visual map generate from it; nothing is hand-copied into prose.

constantNotes.messageMaxBytes: R13/O6: maximum serialized Message JSON bytes. Enforced at validation; over-limit → ValidationFailed. Adjust by editing THIS constant only.
constantNotes.pageLimitMax: Store-Seam §4: paged-read limit is clamped to this, never rejected.
constantNotes.subscriptionBufferMax: R1: per-subscription outbound event buffer. Overflow ends the subscription (ended.reason=overflow); the client re-subscribes with its last cursor.

templateBindablePathsNote: R12: the allowlist. Everything else on Message is core-owned and NOT bindable: id, kind, schemaVersion, createdAt, sequence, threadId, senderId, clientMessageId, template, and all delivery metadata.

PersonId.description: Durable identity, owned by the Identity authority. The only addressable identity (DEC-01). Branded: never interchangeable with other ID kinds.

PresenceId.description: Ephemeral runtime connection (DEC-02). Never an address.

Timestamp.description: Display-only (DEC-19). Nothing in the capability orders by wall-clock.

Sequence.description: Global store sequence (Store-Seam §3). Strictly unique, assigned at commit. Gaps permitted — consumers compare, never count.

Cursor.description: Opaque cursor wrapping the last-seen sequence (Store-Seam §3). Survives restarts. Malformed/foreign → ValidationFailed.

RequestHash.description: SHA-256 hex of the full request content: address, body, priority, template ID + fields (A5). Computed by the core, compared opaquely by the store.

ClientMessageId.description: Client-supplied idempotency key, unique per sender (DEC-13).

Address.description: Typed destination (Plan §8): <kind>:<full durable ID> — e.g. person:person_7f3a, thread:thread_9b2c. person: resolves to the canonical direct Thread (DEC-03). thread: addresses a Thread by ID: for a DIRECT Thread the sender must be one of the canonical pair and the recipient is the other member (R4); for a Room Thread the R4 membership rule applies. Resolved at acceptance.

Priority.description: DEC-12: one field, one policy decision point.

Grant.description: Grants the core may verify via the Authority seam. priority.override is boolean per principal, global in v1 (R10); the role→grant mapping lives in authority-adapter config, never in core (DEC-07 amendment).

TransportKind.description: Presence TRANSPORT adapters in the v1 suite — the outbound delivery effect. The CLI is an inbound protocol adapter (DEC-17), not a presence transport. webhook is deferred (O4).

Message.description: Authoritative. One Message per send, including group sends (DEC-05). Serialized JSON MUST NOT exceed constants.messageMaxBytes (R13).

senderId.description: The authenticated Principal, always (DEC-11, I4, G3). Never caller-supplied.

template.description: Present when the Message was rendered from a template (DEC-15).

Thread.description: Authoritative. Direct: canonical sorted Person pair, one per pair forever (DEC-03). Room: team|mission, referencing exactly one external membership authority (DEC-04).

pair.description: Canonical sorted pair (DEC-03). (me, me) is a valid personal lane (Plan §8 self-send).

authority.description: Name of the external membership authority (Team or Mission capability).

externalId.description: The room's ID in that authority. Membership truth stays with its owner.

DeliveryStateReason.description: Machine-readable reason accompanying a state. delivered → adapter-effect. failed → blocked-by-contact-policy | retry-exhausted | transport-failure.

Delivery.description: Authoritative. One per Message×recipient (DEC-05). State changes only via store CAS (Store-Seam §5). delivered settles only on a real adapter effect (DEC-08, G10, I11).

DeliveryAttempt.description: Authoritative, append-only child of a Delivery (I6). Includes fan-out losers (superseded) so the DEC-16 race is auditable.

outcome.description: effect = real adapter effect (DEC-08). superseded = lost the fan-out CAS race (Store-Seam §5).

detail.description: Adapter-reported failure detail. Never settles state by itself.

Presence.description: Ephemeral (DEC-02). Registered ONLY by explicit OpenPresence — authentication alone never registers (R9). 0..n per Person; duplicate opens are allowed and mint a new Presence each time.

clientLabel.description: Caller-chosen display label. Presentation data, never a durable join (G2).

ContactPolicy.description: Authoritative (DEC-14, A3). Per-recipient send right: allowlist + default rule. Provisioning grants addressability, NOT send-right (A3).

defaultRule.description: deny blocks only senders neither allowlisted nor sharing a Thread with the recipient (DEC-14 implied-allow).

DndPolicy.description: Authoritative. On/off only in v1 (O3); schedules are a later additive field.

field.description: The template-declared field name a sender supplies.

path.description: Target path in the Message schema. MUST be in templateBindablePaths (R12).

Template.description: Authoritative (DEC-15). Bindings render into Message-schema paths; the rendered send validates as SendMessage — templates cannot drift from the contract.

retired.description: Retired templates reject new sends; history unchanged (I10).

revision.description: Opaque membership-authority revision at resolution time (Store-Seam §9, R8 store side).

RecipientSnapshot.description: Authoritative, immutable (I5). Frozen inside the acceptance transaction (DEC-20). Membership changes after acceptance never rewrite it.

blocked.description: R4: room-send recipients whose ContactPolicy blocks the sender. Each gets a terminal failed Delivery; the send itself is accepted. Blocking here is an honesty SIGNAL, not access control — room history remains readable per membership (I10).

membership.description: Room sends only. Frozen with the snapshot (R8 store side, Store-Seam §9).

AcceptanceRecord.description: Authoritative. Durable proof of acceptance, keyed by (senderId, clientMessageId) with requestHash (DEC-13, A5). effectsPending drives the DEC-21 recovery sweep.

effectsPending.description: Written inside the acceptance transaction (DEC-21, Store-Seam §7). Cleared by markEffectsSettled after deliveries, events, and transport scheduling complete.

urgentDowngraded.description: Persisted at acceptance when an urgent send was downgraded (MSG-010). Returned on duplicate retries so the typed outcome survives the retry (DEC-13; Store-Seam §11 errata).

SendMessageInput.description: No sender field exists anywhere — identity comes from authentication only (DEC-11, G3).

fields.description: Values for the template's declared binding fields. Rendered into allowlisted Message paths (R12), then validated as SendMessageInput.

personId.description: Defaults to the caller. Setting another Person's policy requires policy.admin.
Defaults to the caller. Setting another Person's policy requires policy.admin.

templateId.description: Omit to create; supply to revise (expectedRevision semantics per Store-Seam §5).

PresenceClosed.description: Idempotent (R9): closing an unknown or already-closed Presence succeeds — already-closed is the desired end state.

SendAccepted.description: MSG-019: the Message has crossed the durability boundary. A same-key + same-content retry returns THIS original acceptance (DEC-13) — including its urgentDowngraded flag, persisted on the AcceptanceRecord.

urgentDowngraded.description: True when priority=urgent lacked the priority.override grant against a DND recipient — downgraded with a typed outcome, never silently (DEC-07, MSG-010). Survives idempotent retries.

duplicate.description: True when this is the original acceptance returned to a retry (Store-Seam §2 outcome kind=duplicate).

MessagePage.description: Ordered by sequence ascending (DEC-19). limit is clamped to constants.pageLimitMax, never rejected (Store-Seam §4).

limits.description: Values copied from constants by the generator — never hand-written.

CapabilityView.description: Discovery. Callable pre-authentication; reveals versions and limits only.

threads.description: Optional scope. Empty/absent = all threads the subscriber may read (R3). An explicit list naming any Thread the subscriber may NOT read fails the whole Subscribe with NotAuthorized — scope is never silently dropped (G6).

since.description: Optional resume cursor. Replay = committed-fact events with sequence > cursor, in order, then live (R1). Covers MessageCommitted, DeliveryUpdated, and PolicyChanged — the latter two are journaled with sequence per Store-Seam §11 errata.

SubscriptionMessage.description: R1: the Subscribe result stream. Control frames are part of the stream — subscription lifecycle never touches the command error catalogue. Every frame carries subscriptionId so multiple subscriptions can share one connection.

sequence.description: Present on committed-fact events. Consumers dedupe by sequence (at-least-once, R1). Absent on PresenceChanged (observation, R11).

reason.description: overflow = backpressure bound hit (R1): re-subscribe with last cursor; replay closes the gap. closed = transport disconnect. auth-lost = session invalidated. dependency-lost = the journal/store failed mid-stream (DependencyUnavailable class); re-subscribe with last cursor.

commands.name: OpenPresence
commands.summary: Register a live connection for this Person (R9: the ONLY registration mechanism — authentication alone never registers). Naming a transport with no registered adapter fails ValidationFailed (Messaging-Seams §4 composition rule).

commands.name: ClosePresence
commands.summary: Deregister a live connection. Idempotent: unknown/already-closed succeeds. Only the owning Person (or policy.admin) may close; transport-initiated close is always permitted for its own connection (R9).

commands.name: SendMessage
commands.summary: Accept one Message to an address, idempotent by clientMessageId (DEC-13). BlockedByContactPolicy is a DIRECT-send error only; on room sends, blocked recipients become terminal failed Deliveries instead (R4).
commands.authorization: authenticated principal; recipient ContactPolicy. thread:-addressed sends require membership (R4): DIRECT Thread — sender must be one of the canonical pair, recipient is the other member and their ContactPolicy applies; Room Thread — sender membership at acceptance.

commands.name: SendFromTemplate
commands.summary: Render a template's fields into allowlisted Message paths (R12), then accept exactly as SendMessage.

commands.name: SetDndPolicy
commands.summary: Set a Person's DND on/off (O3: no schedules in v1).

commands.name: SetContactPolicy
commands.summary: Set a Person's allowlist + default rule (DEC-14, A3).

commands.name: UpsertTemplate
commands.summary: Create or revise a template. Bindings must target templateBindablePaths only (R12) — violation is ValidationFailed.

commands.name: RetireTemplate
commands.summary: Retire a template. New sends reject with TemplateNotFound; history unchanged (I10).

queries.name: GetThread
queries.authorization: thread member (R3): direct — one of the pair; room — current member per the membership seam

queries.name: ListThreadsForPerson
queries.authorization: self only (R3); policy.admin may list for others

queries.name: GetMessages
queries.summary: Ordered slice of a Thread's history, cursor-based, sequence ascending (DEC-19).

queries.name: GetInbox
queries.summary: Messages awaiting a Person — Deliveries in pending or held state ONLY. Terminal states (delivered, failed) never appear, so a room-blocked recipient (R4) is not served the blocked Message here. DND holds attention, never access (guarantee 6).
queries.authorization: self only (R3); policy.admin may act for others

queries.name: GetDelivery
queries.summary: Per-recipient delivery state for one Message (MSG-016: failure truth without an agent turn).

queries.name: GetPresence
queries.authorization: any authenticated principal (R3) — presence is observability, not addressing

queries.name: GetCapabilities
queries.summary: Protocol version + supported features + limits. Discovery for hosts whose deployments may differ.
queries.authorization: none — callable pre-authentication (R3); reveals versions and limits only

subscriptions.name: Subscribe
subscriptions.summary: R1: the push contract (MSG-007, MSG-023). A connected principal receives committed-fact events pushed over its live Presence — polling is a catch-up fallback after disconnect, never the liveness mechanism.
subscriptions.authorization: any authenticated principal; event payload filtered to threads the subscriber may read (R3). An explicit threads[] naming a Thread the subscriber may NOT read fails the whole Subscribe with NotAuthorized — scope is never silently dropped (G6).

result.description: A STREAM of SubscriptionMessage frames: started → event* → ended. Every frame carries subscriptionId.

subscriptions.scope: events filter (required) + optional threads scope; empty threads = all threads the subscriber may read
subscriptions.cursor: Optional opaque sequence cursor (Store-Seam §3). Replay-after-disconnect: committed-fact events with sequence > cursor, in order via the journal, then live. Delivery transitions and policy writes are journaled with sequence (Store-Seam §11 errata), so replay covers all three committed-fact event kinds.
subscriptions.duplicates: At-least-once. Committed-fact events carry their sequence; the consumer dedupes by sequence. Exactly-once is never promised.
subscriptions.backpressure: Bounded per-subscription buffer (constants.subscriptionBufferMax). Overflow ENDS the subscription with ended.reason=overflow — the core never blocks on a slow subscriber. The client re-subscribes with its last cursor; replay closes the gap.
subscriptions.observations: PresenceChanged is an observation, not a committed fact (R11): it carries no sequence, is not journaled, and is never replayed. On (re)subscribe, current presence state is sent as fresh observations.

events.name: MessageCommitted
events.summary: A Message crossed the durability boundary. Emitted only after commit (§13 event rule). Carries the full Message.
events.audience: subscribers authorized to read the message's thread (R3)

events.name: DeliveryUpdated
events.summary: A per-recipient Delivery changed state, carrying state + reason. Failure states included — DeliveryFailed is folded into this event (MSG-016). Journaled with sequence per Store-Seam §11 errata, so subscription replay covers it.
events.audience: subscribers authorized to read the delivery's thread (R3)

events.name: PresenceChanged
events.summary: R11: a Presence opened/closed. Presence is ephemeral, so this is an OBSERVATION — no sequence, not journaled, never replayed. The durability-before-emission rule applies to committed-fact events only.

events.name: PolicyChanged
events.summary: A DND or contact policy changed (policy writes are durable, so this is a committed fact). Journaled with sequence per Store-Seam §11 errata.

errors.name: NotAuthorized
errors.summary: Authenticated, but lacks the grant, membership, or ownership this operation requires (R3 matrix).

errors.name: UnknownRecipient
errors.summary: The address does not resolve to a provisioned Person (MSG-014).

errors.name: UnknownThread
errors.summary: No such Thread, including room Threads unknown at acceptance (Store-Seam §2.1).

errors.name: BlockedByContactPolicy
errors.summary: DIRECT sends only: the recipient's ContactPolicy blocks this sender. Room sends instead record terminal failed Deliveries per blocked recipient (R4).

errors.name: ValidationFailed
errors.summary: Input failed schema or policy validation — including over messageMaxBytes (R13) and malformed/foreign cursors (Store-Seam §6 CursorInvalid mapping).

errors.name: TemplateNotFound
errors.summary: No such template, or it is retired.

errors.name: TemplateFieldMismatch
errors.summary: Supplied fields do not match the template's declared bindings (DEC-15).

errors.name: VersionUnsupported
errors.summary: The client speaks a protocol/contract version this deployment does not serve.

errors.name: RateLimited
errors.summary: FORWARD-RESERVED (R13, O2): no send rate limits in v1. The shape exists in the catalogue but appears in no per-operation failure list until O2 activates.

errors.name: IdempotencyConflict
errors.summary: A5: same (senderId, clientMessageId) but different requestHash. Pass-through from the store seam — public by design.

errors.name: DependencyUnavailable
errors.summary: R6: typed public outcome for dependency failure. One umbrella shape; the dependency field names which seam failed. StoreUnavailable/StorageExhausted/StoreCorrupt map here (Store-Seam §6); membership-timeout and authority-failure reuse THIS shape (Messaging-Seams §2.2, §3.3); clock/ID halt-class failures use dependency=clock (Messaging-Seams §5.2). presence-transport is DELIBERATELY absent — its failures surface through the Delivery lane as typed state, a richer public outcome (Messaging-Seams §4.2). Consumers assume non-retryable unless the instance's retryable field says true; they MUST tolerate unknown dependency values (treat as non-retryable).

dependency.description: Known values: store | membership | authority | clock (clock added at Step 3b). Typed as open string, NOT an enum — additive extension is the compatibility rule and consumers MUST tolerate unknown values (treat as non-retryable). presence-transport is deliberately absent (failures surface via the Delivery lane, Messaging-Seams §4.2).

retryable.description: Per-instance flag. false for StoreCorrupt-class failures — operator intervention required. Absent/unknown → assume false.

errorNotes.derivation: 11 named in Plan §9 + IdempotencyConflict (A5) + DependencyUnavailable (R6) = 13. RateLimited is forward-reserved (R13). The 11-vs-12 doc drift is resolved HERE at the source — this array is the only count that exists.
errorNotes.notPublic: StateConflict and RevisionConflict (Store-Seam §6) are normal concurrency outcomes handled inside the core; they never cross the public contract. RecordNotFound maps to UnknownThread/UnknownMessage/etc. CursorInvalid maps to ValidationFailed.

transitions.note: Recipient DND is on and the priority does not override (normal, or urgent downgraded for lack of the grant). The Message remains pullable via GetInbox — DND holds attention, never access.

A real transport effect on one of the recipient's live Presences (DEC-08, G10, I11). Fan-out first-success race resolves at the store CAS (Store-Seam §5): first effect wins; losers are recorded as superseded attempts.
Terminal AT ACCEPTANCE (R4): room-send recipient whose ContactPolicy blocks the sender. No attempts are ever made.
The adapter's bounded retry budget (adapter config; v1 default 5 attempts with backoff) ran out.
The adapter reports a non-retryable failure (e.g. PTY gone permanently). No further retries.
SetDndPolicy(enabled=false) releases every held Delivery for that Person back to pending; normal delivery attempts resume.

An attempt STARTED before the hold reports a real adapter effect after the Delivery moved to held. The effect genuinely occurred (DEC-08) and cannot be un-rung: it settles delivered. This is the one legal exit from held other than dnd-released; the attempt is recorded with outcome effect.

delivery.noPresence: A recipient with zero live Presences leaves the Delivery in pending — NOT failed (there is nothing to retry against, and v1 has no expiry, O1). Each PresenceChanged(opened) for that recipient re-triggers an attempt decision by the effect shell.
delivery.policyEvaluation: DND and contact policy are re-evaluated at EVERY attempt decision point — acceptance, presence-open re-trigger, and each retry — against CURRENT policy, never a value cached from acceptance. A presence-open re-trigger during active DND moves pending→held instead of attempting.
delivery.urgentOverride: Urgent WITH the priority.override grant skips held entirely: pending → delivery attempt immediately, DND notwithstanding (DEC-07, I9).
delivery.heldNeverFails: held has no failure transitions: no attempts run while held, so retries cannot exhaust. held exits only via dnd-released or in-flight-effect.
